```r
# count NaN for each column
count_na_per_column <- function(data) {
  sapply(data, function(col) sum(is.na(col)))}

count_na_per_column_df <- function(data) {
  na_counts <- sapply(data, function(col) sum(is.na(col)))
  na_counts_df <- data.frame(
    feature = names(na_counts),
    na_count = na_counts
  )
  na_counts_df %>% arrange(desc(na_count))
}

# extract first genre for the spotify genre
extract_first_genre <- function(df, genre_column = "spotify_genre") {
  # check if column exists
  if (!genre_column %in% colnames(df)) {
    stop(paste("La colonna", genre_column, "non esiste nel dataframe"))
  }
  
  # removes useless not required characters
  df[[genre_column]] <- gsub("\\[|\\]|'", "", df[[genre_column]])
  
  # create a list, with div = ,
  genre_list <- strsplit(df[[genre_column]], split = ",")
  
  # extract only the first genre for each line or rename "others"
  df$first_genre <- sapply(genre_list, function(x) {
    x <- trimws(x)  # remove blanks
    if (length(x) == 0 || is.na(x[1]) || x[1] == "") {
      return("others")
    } else {
      return(x[1])
    }
  })
  
  # convert to categorical value
  df$first_genre <- as.factor(df$first_genre)
  
  # output
  return(df)
}

# process and encode the genre column
process_and_encode_genre <- function(df, genre_column = "first_genre", top_n = 15) {
  # check if column exists
  if (!genre_column %in% colnames(df)) {
    stop(paste("La colonna", genre_column, "non esiste nel dataframe"))
  }
  
  # count the frequency
  genre_counts <- table(df[[genre_column]])
  
  # put them in decrescent order
  genre_counts_sorted <- sort(genre_counts, decreasing = TRUE)
  
  # take top N genres
  top_genres <- names(genre_counts_sorted)[1:min(top_n, length(genre_counts_sorted))]
  
  # rename not in top N into 'others'
  df[[genre_column]] <- ifelse(
    df[[genre_column]] %in% top_genres,
    df[[genre_column]],
    "others"
  )
  
  # convert
  df[[genre_column]] <- as.factor(df[[genre_column]])
  
  # remove original column
  if ("spotify_genre" %in% colnames(df)) {
    df <- subset(df, select = -c(spotify_genre))
  }
  
  # create dummy variables (one-hot encoding)
  dummy <- dummyVars(paste("~", genre_column), data = df)
  dummy_df <- data.frame(predict(dummy, newdata = df))
  
  final_df <- bind_cols(
    df %>% select(-all_of(genre_column)),
    dummy_df
  )
  
  # output
  return(final_df)
}

# encode popularity column
encode_spotify_popularity <- function(df, column = "spotify_track_popularity") {
  # check if column exists
  if (!column %in% colnames(df)) {
    stop(paste("La colonna", column, "non esiste nel dataframe"))
  }
  
  categorize_popularity <- function(x) {
    if (is.na(x)) return(NA)
    if (x <= 25) {
      return("low")
    } else if (x <= 50) {
      return("medium")
    } else if (x <= 75) {
      return("high")
    } else if (x <= 100) {
      return("very high")
    } else {
      return(NA)  # out of range
    }
  }
  
  df[[column]] <- sapply(df[[column]], categorize_popularity)
  
  # convert in ordered factor
  df[[column]] <- factor(df[[column]], 
                         levels = c("low", "medium", "high", "very high"), 
                         ordered = TRUE)
  
  # output
  return(df)
}

# plots the confusion matrix
plot_conf_matrix <- function(conf_matrix_object, title = "Confusion Matrix") {
  
  # converts confusion matrix into dataframe
  cm_df <- as.data.frame(conf_matrix_object$table)
  
  # find columns names (Truth, Prediction, Freq)
  colnames(cm_df) <- tolower(colnames(cm_df)) # rende tutto minuscolo
  
  # rename them
  names(cm_df)[names(cm_df) %in% c("reference", "truth")] <- "Actual"
  names(cm_df)[names(cm_df) == "prediction"] <- "Predicted"
  names(cm_df)[names(cm_df) %in% c("freq", "n")] <- "Freq"
  
  # plot
  p <- ggplot(cm_df, aes(x = Predicted, y = Actual, fill = Freq)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_text(aes(label = Freq), size = 5, color = "black") +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "steelblue") +
    labs(title = title,
         x = "Predicted Class",
         y = "Actual Class",
         fill = "Count") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"))
  
  return(p)
}
```

  group_by(variable, value) |>
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(variable) |>
  slice_max(order_by = count, n = 50)

# barplot distribution facet

  geom_col(fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +

  group_by(song_id) %>%
  summarise(

    avg_position = mean(week_position),
    weeks_in_chart = n_distinct(week_id),
    final_position = last(week_position)
  )

full_data_aggregate <- merge(billboard_summary, audio_features, by = "song_id", all = FALSE)
full_data_aggregate <- full_data_aggregate %>% select(-c(instrumentalness, time_signature))

#### Regression


<!-- rnb-text-end -->


<!-- rnb-chunk-begin -->


<!-- rnb-output-begin  -->


<!-- rnb-source-begin  -->

```r

set.seed(45)
split <- initial_split(head(regression_data_encoded,100), prop = 0.8)
train_data <- training(split)
test_data  <- testing(split)

# recipe
#recipe_spec <- recipe(spotify_track_popularity ~ ., data = train_data)
recipe_spec <- recipe(spotify_track_popularity ~ ., data = train_data) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE)

# define models
task = 'regression'

models <- list(
  rf = rand_forest(mtry = 5) %>% set_engine("randomForest") %>% set_mode(task),
  #lm = linear_reg() %>% set_engine("lm") %>% set_mode(task),
  xgb = boost_tree(trees = 1000, tree_depth = 10) %>% set_engine("xgboost") %>% set_mode(task),
  knn = nearest_neighbor(neighbors = 5) %>% set_engine("kknn") %>% set_mode(task)
)

# workflow list
workflows_list <- purrr::map(models, ~ workflow() %>% add_model(.x) %>% add_recipe(recipe_spec))

# train the models
fitted_models <- purrr::map(workflows_list, ~ fit(.x, data = train_data))

# evaluation
results <- purrr::map(fitted_models, ~ {
  predict(.x, test_data) %>%
    bind_cols(test_data) %>%
    metrics(truth = spotify_track_popularity, estimate = .pred)
})

# results
results_df <- bind_rows(results, .id = "model")

results_df %>%
  filter(.metric == "rmse") %>%
  arrange(.estimate)

print(results_df)
```

<!-- rnb-source-end -->


<!-- rnb-output-end -->

<!-- rnb-chunk-end -->


<!-- rnb-text-begin -->



<!-- rnb-text-end -->


<!-- rnb-chunk-begin -->


<!-- rnb-output-begin  -->


<!-- rnb-source-begin  -->

```r
results <- list()

for (model_name in names(fitted_models)) {
  model <- models[[model_name]]
  
  wf <- workflow() %>%
    add_model(model) %>%
    add_recipe(recipe_spec)
  
  fit_model <- fit(wf, data = train_data)
  
  preds <- predict(fit_model, test_data) %>%
    bind_cols(test_data) %>%
    mutate(model = model_name)
  
  results[[model_name]] <- preds
}

all_predictions <- bind_rows(results)

```

<!-- rnb-source-end -->


<!-- rnb-output-end -->

<!-- rnb-chunk-end -->


<!-- rnb-text-begin -->



<!-- rnb-text-end -->


<!-- rnb-chunk-begin -->


<!-- rnb-output-begin  -->


<!-- rnb-source-begin  -->

```r

ggplot(all_predictions, aes(x = spotify_track_popularity, y = .pred)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~model, scales = "free") +
  labs(
    title = "Predictions vs Real Values",
    x = "Real Values (spotify_track_popularity)",
    y = "Predictions"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```r
registerDoParallel(cores = parallel::detectCores() - 1)

set.seed(42)

# 1. Split
split <- initial_split(df_filtered_2000_15_genre_encoded, prop = 0.8)
#split <- initial_split(regression_data_encoded_scaled, prop = 0.8)
train_data <- training(split)
test_data  <- testing(split)

# 2. Recipe
recipe_spec <- recipe(spotify_track_popularity ~ ., data = train_data) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE)

# 3. Resampling
cv_folds <- vfold_cv(train_data, v = 5)

# 4. Define the models with the parameters to tune
models <- list(
  rf = rand_forest(mtry = tune(), trees = 1000) %>%
    set_engine("randomForest") %>% set_mode("regression"),

  xgb = boost_tree(trees = 1000, tree_depth = tune(), learn_rate = tune()) %>%
    set_engine("xgboost") %>% set_mode("regression"),

  knn = nearest_neighbor(neighbors = tune()) %>%
    set_engine("kknn") %>% set_mode("regression")
)

# 5. Create workflows
workflows_list <- purrr::imap(models, function(model, name) {
  workflow() %>%
    add_model(model) %>%
    add_recipe(recipe_spec)
})

# 6. Tuning with tune_race_anova
tuned_models <- purrr::imap(workflows_list, function(wf, name) {
  tune_race_anova(
    wf,
    resamples = cv_folds,
    grid = 5,
    metrics = metric_set(rmse),
    control = control_race(verbose_elim = TRUE)
  )
})

# 7. Exctract the best hiperparameters
best_models <- purrr::map(tuned_models, ~ select_best(.x))

# 8. Finalize and fit
final_models <- purrr::map2(workflows_list, best_models, ~ finalize_workflow(.x, .y) %>% fit(data = train_data))

# 9. Evaluate on test set
results <- purrr::map(final_models, ~ {
  predict(.x, test_data) %>%
    bind_cols(test_data) %>%
    metrics(truth = spotify_track_popularity, estimate = .pred)
})

# 10. RMSE results
results_df <- bind_rows(results, .id = "model") %>%
  filter(.metric == "rmse") %>%
  arrange(.estimate)

print(results_df)
```

<!-- rnb-source-end -->


<!-- rnb-output-end -->

<!-- rnb-chunk-end -->

#Hypothesis test

##Have songs from the last ten years become louder than before?
We chose to perform this hypothesis test on the loudness because we noticed it was the most important feature among all the audio features of the songs.


<!-- rnb-text-end -->


<!-- rnb-chunk-begin -->


<!-- rnb-output-begin  -->


<!-- rnb-source-begin  -->

```r
#selecting only the numeric features
numeric_data_after_2000 <- df_filtered_2000_15_genre_encoded |>
  select(where(is.numeric))

#selecting all the features that are not related to the genre
numeric_data_after_2000 <- numeric_data_after_2000 |>
  select(1:(ncol(numeric_data_after_2000) - 27))
par(mfrow = c(2,2))


#plotting the QQ plots to show the distribution of the dataset
for (colname in names(numeric_data_after_2000)) {
  qqnorm(numeric_data_after_2000[[colname]], main = paste("QQ Plot -", colname))
  qqline(numeric_data_after_2000[[colname]])
}
```

<!-- rnb-source-end -->


<!-- rnb-output-end -->

<!-- rnb-chunk-end -->


<!-- rnb-text-begin -->



<!-- rnb-text-end -->


<!-- rnb-chunk-begin -->


<!-- rnb-output-begin  -->


<!-- rnb-source-begin  -->

```r
#selecting only the numeric features
numeric_data_before_2015 <- df_filtered_before_2015_genre_encoded |>
  select(where(is.numeric))

#selecting all the features that are not related to the genre
numeric_data_before_2015 <- numeric_data_before_2015 |>
  select(1:(ncol(numeric_data_before_2015) - 27))
par(mfrow = c(2,2))

#plotting the QQ plots to show the distribution of the dataset
for (colname in names(numeric_data_before_2015)) {
  qqnorm(numeric_data_before_2015[[colname]], main = paste("QQ Plot -", colname))
  qqline(numeric_data_before_2015[[colname]])
}
```

<!-- rnb-source-end -->


<!-- rnb-output-end -->

<!-- rnb-chunk-end -->


<!-- rnb-text-begin -->

Based on the QQ plots for the periods before and after 2015, none of the feature distributions appear to be normal. Therefore, to compare the two distributions, we should use the Wilcoxon test.


<!-- rnb-text-end -->


<!-- rnb-chunk-begin -->


<!-- rnb-output-begin  -->


<!-- rnb-source-begin  -->

```r

#Doing a wilcox test based on the loudness of the songs
wilcox.test(
  df_filtered_2000_15_genre_encoded$loudness,
  df_filtered_before_2015_genre_encoded$loudness,
  alternative = "greater"
)
```

<!-- rnb-source-end -->


<!-- rnb-output-end -->

<!-- rnb-output-begin  -->

```

	Wilcoxon rank sum test with continuity correction

data:  df_filtered_2000_15_genre_encoded$loudness and df_filtered_before_2015_genre_encoded$loudness
W = 29527014, p-value < 2.2e-16
alternative hypothesis: true location shift is greater than 0
```



<!-- rnb-output-end -->

<!-- rnb-output-begin  -->


<!-- rnb-source-begin  -->
